hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained, Florida Forest Service warns more expected this summer
hero.body:
Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both fires are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said the department is in peak fire season. The summer heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them ready to ignite when lightning strikes occur. Grubitch explained that while rain often extinguishes these fires immediately, sometimes they travel underground and surface days later.

The Florida Forest Service said the conditions that fuel these fires are not going away anytime soon, but residents should not be alarmed. The department expects more brush fires to occur throughout the summer months due to the hot, dry conditions and frequent lightning strikes during afternoon thunderstorms.

Grubitch stressed that the public plays a crucial role in helping the Florida Forest Service do its job. He said residents should never assume someone else has already called in a brush fire. If residents see smoke or fire, they should report it immediately, as early notification can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County woman accused of using vehicle to assault three people
cards.teaser: Tioniea Hines, 22, is being held in St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond.
cards.body:
Tioniea Hines, 22, was arrested and charged with three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. She is accused of using her vehicle in an assault on three people.

Hines is currently being held in St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond. The aggravated battery charges involve using a deadly weapon during the alleged assault.

The case involves allegations that Hines used her vehicle as a weapon against three individuals. Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon is a serious felony charge in Florida that applies when a person intentionally causes bodily harm to another using an object capable of causing death or great harm.

No additional details about the circumstances of the alleged assault, the condition of the victims, or the specific events leading to the charges have been released. Hines remains in custody as the case proceeds through the legal system.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida Home Insurance Market Shows Signs of Recovery as Carriers Return
cards.body:
Florida's troubled home insurance market is showing signs of improvement as more insurance companies return to the state and some rates begin to decline. The development marks a potential turning point for homeowners who have faced years of rising premiums and limited coverage options.

Insurance carriers are gradually re-entering the Florida market after years of departures driven by hurricane losses and financial instability. The return of additional insurers is creating more competition in a market that has been dominated by a shrinking number of providers. Some homeowners are beginning to see rate decreases as the expanded carrier presence takes effect. The changes follow legislative reforms aimed at stabilizing the insurance industry in Florida.

The insurance crisis has affected homeowners statewide, with many forced to turn to Citizens Property Insurance Corporation, the state-backed insurer of last resort, as private carriers withdrew from the market. Premium costs had surged to among the highest in the nation, with some residents paying triple the national average for coverage. The market instability left hundreds of thousands of Florida property owners struggling to secure affordable protection against hurricane damage and other perils. The consequences of lacking coverage were illustrated when Hurricane Milton tore the roof off a Florida home just two months after the owner had paid off his mortgage, leaving him to cover repair costs entirely out of pocket.

The recovery remains fragile as insurers continue to assess their exposure to Florida's hurricane risk. Companies returning to the market are evaluating their capacity to handle potential storm losses while maintaining financial stability. Heritage Insurance is among the carriers navigating the challenging Florida market, with the company's stock holding steady as it manages hurricane exposure in the state. Industry observers note that sustained improvement will depend on continued reforms and the state's hurricane activity in coming seasons. The expanded carrier presence offers hope for homeowners who have endured years of market turmoil and escalating costs.

cards.headline: Czech tennis player Linda Noskova wins Wimbledon after recovering from blown match points
cards.teaser: Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy.
cards.body:
Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. The 21-year-old Noskova became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024.

Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance, as was Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club. Navratilova looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner wins second straight Wimbledon title, defeats Alexander Zverev
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7, 7-6, 6-3, 6-4 Sunday for his second consecutive title at the All England Club and fifth Grand Slam title overall.
cards.body:
Jannik Sinner claimed his fifth Grand Slam title in his first tournament since a second-round meltdown at the French Open, when he wilted in a Paris heat wave. The top-ranked player ripped a forehand winner up the line on his first match point and dropped to the grass on his back in celebration. A year ago, Sinner beat Carlos Alcaraz in the final at the All England Club after wasting three match points against his rival in the Roland Garros final.

Zverev appeared bothered by a knee issue following a slip to the grass on a key point in the third set. At 3-3 in the third set, 2 hours and 42 minutes in, Sinner produced a drop shot and Zverev slipped and appeared to hyper-extend his right knee as he attempted to change directions behind the baseline. Zverev grasped his knee in apparent discomfort and Sinner went around the net and helped his opponent up off the grass. Zverev appeared slightly hampered after the slip and slung his racket across the baseline in frustration when he missed a forehand and handed Sinner the first break of the match and a 5-3 lead in the third.

It was Sinner's 10th straight victory over Zverev, who was coming off his first Grand Slam title at the French Open. Prince William joined his wife Kate and two of their children for the final in a star-studded Royal Box that also included actors Dustin Hoffman, Nicole Kidman and Ben Stiller. Despite the defeat in the final, Zverev will leapfrog Alcaraz into the No. 2 spot in the rankings on Monday.

cards.headline: Karolina Muchova defeats Coco Gauff at Wimbledon in dramatic tiebreaker
cards.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker to reach the final.
cards.body:
The ninth-ranked Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker. The win makes Muchova the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, who was runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, who won the championship in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, who won the championship in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova set to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court.

cards.headline: Park Vista football team aims for state playoffs after strong late-season finish
cards.teaser: Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026 after winning four of their last five games in 2025.
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The Cobras struggled to find their footing early in 2025, but finished strong, winning four of their last five games. Senior Harris Bender said it felt good throughout the second half of that season. The team is working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, and Bender said the Cobras have all the pieces in place now and it is just about executing. The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017.

Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna said the team has to take it one game at a time and cannot look past anyone. Hanna said the Cobras have to handle business weekly, and if they do that and do their job, that will get them in the playoffs. Senior Erik Lee said he feels like the team has the guys they need to get it done, but the Cobras also have to put the work in to get there as well. Senior Justice Jones said it is going to feel amazing because he already knows it is going to happen. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17
hero.teaser:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Driv
hero.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance work continues on several major roadways. The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions, with additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on drivers.

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from 8 p.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16. Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road for roadway construction. The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will also be closed from 8 p.m. Sunday through Thursday for paving and lighting installation. Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue. Weather-related contingency dates for both closures are scheduled for July 19-23.

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project, beginning at 7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continuing until 5 p.m. Friday, July 17. Portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time and access to homes and businesses will be maintained. Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads depending on the closure location. Additional lane closures are planned on SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road during daytime hours Monday through Friday, with two lanes potentially closing overnight for drainage work, milling and repaving.

Motorists should also expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line, with up to two lanes closing in each direction for milling, resurfacing and signage work. The existing A1A North Causeway drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Friday as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge, though vehicle traffic on the new bridge will not be affected. Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions, and motorists should allow additional travel time and use caution around workers and equipment.
